Deployed direct-fill acceptance and pilot boundaries #398

offers.label: Wallet-derived encryption for IPFS snapshots
offers.detail: Snapshots are encrypted in the browser with AES-GCM using an HKDF key derived from a wallet signature over a fixed purpose message, bound to the address as additional data. Uploads are refused when a wallet's signature is not repeatable; legacy plaintext snapshots still restore. Node tests cover round trip, wrong wallet and tampering; live-provider restore is not verified.

offers.label: Direct-fill Genie nutrition and shared food references
offers.detail: PR #404 (issue #403) replaces strict source-only refusal with practical best estimates: Genie fills the existing editable nutrition card directly, and a blank card auto-fills once food, amount and unit are entered (community library first, then one Genie call for invited wallets; typed figures are never overwritten). One structured call weighs the 3-4 most plausible interpretations, states its assumption, estimates homemade foods from main ingredients and estimates household portions; there is no clarification dialog and no separate review window. Cards are labeled Genie estimate unless every value and portion comes from a verified searched source (web search only for packaged products). Labeled estimates and source-backed cards enter a durable public library, reusable across fresh browsers without a wallet or provider call; an estimate never replaces a source-backed card. Personal edits, defaults, meals and health records are not uploaded to that library. Manual review/defaults remain available without Genie access, under the unchanged shared cap. Earlier work: #399 direct fill, #397 cited search, #401 source-linked household portions and fractional cup/serving arithmetic; without a portion measure one serving explicitly means the card base, and volume ratios use US nutrition-label units; personal overrides are never published. Earlier separate deployed synthetic acceptance in #390 covered cooked chickpeas and an exact yogurt product. Current deployed acceptance in #403: homemade yogurt per tbsp, cooked chickpeas and plain pasta per cup each filled in about 2-4 s with one call, were shared as estimates with persistence after redeployment, and the live app auto-filled a blank pasta card from the library with no AI call. That scoped evidence is not whole-food/product coverage, independent nutrient or current-label certification, automatic freshness or synonym coverage, or health-profile synchronization; estimates are approximate food-logging figures.
